items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the play 'Wisdom Paves the Way', and answer.

"The dust on the road told its own tale. The footprints were deep on one side and light on the other. Leaves had been nibbled from the bushes on the left, but those on the right were untouched. The youngest brother knelt, looked closely and said, 'Whoever passed here was in no hurry, and saw only one side of the road.'"

Answer the following:
(i) Which bushes had been nibbled?  (a) The bushes on the right  (b) All the bushes  (c) The bushes on the left  (d) None of the bushes
(ii) What did the youngest brother conclude?
(iii) The skill shown by the youngest brother is …  (a) deduction from observation  (b) telling a lie  (c) blind guessing  (d) singing a song
(iv) What does "the dust on the road told its own tale" mean?
items.answer: (i) (c) The bushes on the left (ii) That whoever passed was in no hurry and saw only one side of the road. (iii) (a) deduction from observation (iv) The marks in the dust gave information about what had passed – the road "spoke" through clues.
items.markingKey: (i) (c) The bushes on the left (ii) That whoever passed was in no hurry and saw only one side of the road. (iii) (a) deduction from observation (iv) The marks in the dust gave information about what had passed – the road "spoke" through clues. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)

"The court fell silent as the eldest brother finished his account. 'We never saw the animal, Your Majesty,' he said. 'We only read the road as a scholar reads a book.' The king leaned forward, a slow smile spreading across his face. 'Then you have taught my whole court a lesson today,' he said."
